Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue West Triangle, Quezon City 1100 DILG Legal Opinion NO. 45 S. 2015 NOV 11 2015 HON. VICENTE HOMER B. REVIL Acting Governor Masbate Dear Hon. Revil: This has reference to your letter dated 04 October 2015, which we received on 20 October 2015, on the following queries: Whether or not the word 'public' as used in Section 5(a) of RA 6713 includes people like Mr. Alden Almero: a. b. c. d. e. Who is not inside Philippine territory; Whose identity and whereabouts are uncertain/unknown,• Who might not be a Filipino citizen; Who, in most probability, might not even be a taxpayer of the Repu blic of the Philippines; and Who has already been making false accusations, maligning, insulting, dishonouring, and discrediting publicly (in social media) the public official concerned? 2. 3. 4. Whether or not the letter-inquiries forwarded by DILG OIC Director Pastor considering the circuxnstances surrounding the same as above- revealed, are within the meaning OT the 'letters' contemplated by Section 5 (a) of RA 6713? Does Section 5 (a) of RA 6713 indeed require the undersigned to act on or to respond to the said letter-inquiries, especially by answering the specific questions therein asked? Does Section 5 (a) of RA 6713 require the undersigned to respondent to or act on all letter-inquiries, that is, absolutely or regardless of circumstances?" Section 5 (a) of Republic Act No. 6713 or the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees (hereinafter, "Code") states:

"Section 5. Duties of Public Officials and Employees. - In the performance of' their duties, all public officials and employees are under obligation to: (a) Act promptly on letters and requests. - All public officials and employees shall, within fifteen (15) working days from receipt thereof. respond to etters tele rams or other means ofcommunicationssent b the u Ii . The reply must contain the action taken on the request. xxv (Emphasis Supplied) In your first query, you are seeking clarification on whether the word "public" in the aforequoted provision of the Code includes people like Mr. Alden Almero, who, according to you, is not inside the Philippine territory, has uncertain/unknown identity and whereabouts, is not a Filipino citizen, not a taxpayer and is making false accusations and similar acts against you. We answer in the affirmative. It is relevant to note that Section 5 (a) of the Code did not make a qualification on who should be included in the term "public". Ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguire debemus. When the law does not distinguish, we must not distinguish. Along this line, in the case Subido vs. Ozaetal, the Supreme Court had an opportunity to construe the term "public"in this manner: '"Public' is a comprehensive, all-inclusive term. Properly construed, it embraces every person. To say that only those who have a present and existing interest of a pecuniary character in the particular information sought are given the right of inspection is to make an unwarranted distinction. This interpretation is contrary to the letter of the law and the whole concept and purpose of registration of recorded titles, which is to serve notice to all who might be affected by the registries. " (Emphasis Supplied) As to your second query, we again reply in the affirmative. The word "letter" has been defined as "a written message addressed to some person and sent to him '7. As to your third and fourth queries, may we invite your attention to the following provisions of the Rules Implementing the Code, thus: "Section 3. In case ofwritten requests, petitions or motions, sent by means of letters, telegrams, or the like, the official or employee in charge shall act on the same within fifteen (15) working days from receipt thereof, provided that: G.R. No. L-1631, 27 February 1948. 2 Philippine Legal Encyclopedia, Jose Agaton R. Sibal, p. 511 (1986).

(a) Ifthe communication is within the jurisdiction of the office or agency, the official or employee must: (1) Write a note or letter of acknowledgement where the matter is merely routinary or the action desired may be acted upon in the ordinary course of business of the department, office or agency, specifying the date when the matter will be disposed of and the name of the official or employee in charge thereof (2) Where the matter is non-routinary or the issues involved are not simple or ordinary, write a note or letter of acknowledgement, informing the interested party, petitioner or correspondent of the action to be taken or when such requests, petitions or motions can be acted upon. Where there is a need to submit additional information, requirements, or documents, the note or letter of acknowledgment shall so state, specifying reasonable period of time within which they should be submitted, and the name of the particular official or employee in charge thereof When all the documents or requirements have been submitted to the satisfaction of the department, or office of agency concerned, the particular official or employee in charge shall inform the interested party, petitioner, or correspondent of the action to be taken and when such action or disposition can be expected, barring unforeseen circumstances. (b) [fcommunication is outside itsjurisdiction, the official or employee must: (1) Refer the letter, petition, telegram, or verbal request to the proper department, office or agency. (2) Acknowledge the communication by means of note or letter, informing the interested party, petitioner, or correspondent of the action taken and attaching a copy of the letter of referral to the proper department, office or agency. The department, office and agency to which the letter, petition, telegram or verbal request was referred for appropriate action must take action in accordance with subsection (a), pars. I & 2 hereof. The period of fifteen (15) days herein provided shall be counted from date of receipt of the written or verbal communication by the department, office or agency concerned. " As can be reasonably deduced from the foregoing, the concerned official or employee is required to respond to the request within fifteen (15) working days but not

ssarily to complete the action or resolve completely the issues involved particularly if the "matter is non-routinary or the issues involved are not simple or ordinary". We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. V ruly yours, AUSTERE A. PAN Undersecretary RO 1.11s/17 Copy furnished: ARD ELOUISA T. PASTOR Officer-in-Charge DILG-Region V Rizal St., Legazpi City
